record.original_question: Determine whether there exists a model of computation in which the Invariance Theorem remains valid for time complexity as well.

evidence.quote: 18. Is there any model of computation in which the Invariance Theorem holds true also for the time complexity? (C. Calude)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Fix an effective enumeration of partial computable functions and, for any (partial) computable function $\varphi:\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}^*$, define the description complexity relative to $\varphi$ by
$$C_\varphi(x)\;=\;\min\{\,|p|\,:\,\varphi(p)=x\,\},$$
with $C_\varphi(x)=\infty$ if no such $p$ exists. The classical Invariance Theorem states that there exists a "universal" partial computable function $U$ such that for every partial computable $\varphi$ there is a constant $c_\varphi$ with
$$C_U(x)\;\le\;C_\varphi(x)+c_\varphi\qquad\text{for all }x\in\{0,1\}^*.$$
Equivalently, $C_U$ is minimal up to an additive constant among all $C_\varphi$.

Now consider a time-bounded analogue. Given a model of computation $\mathcal{M}$ in which programs run on inputs and have a well-defined running time $\mathrm{time}_\varphi(p)$, define a time-sensitive description complexity, e.g.
$$C^t_\varphi(x)\;=\;\min\{\,|p|\,:\,\varphi(p)=x\text{ and }\mathrm{time}_\varphi(p)\le t(|x|)\,\},$$
or, more generally, a complexity measure that simultaneously accounts for program length and computation time.

Question. Does there exist a model of computation $\mathcal{M}$, together with a notion of time complexity in $\mathcal{M}$, such that an Invariance Theorem holds for the time-bounded complexity? That is, does there exist in $\mathcal{M}$ a universal program $U$ such that for every program $\varphi$ in $\mathcal{M}$ there is a constant $c_\varphi$ (independent of $x$) with the time-bounded complexity satisfying
$$C^{\,\text{time}}_U(x)\;\le\;C^{\,\text{time}}_\varphi(x)+c_\varphi\qquad\text{for all }x,$$
in direct analogy with the classical (length-only) Invariance Theorem?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem attributed to C. Calude in the CDMTCS research report on open problems in algorithmic information theory. Web searches did not surface a published resolution; standard references (Wikipedia on Kolmogorov complexity, Scholarpedia on algorithmic complexity, and surveys on invariance and universality of complexity) discuss only the classical (length-only) Invariance Theorem and the well-known additive overhead phenomenon for time-bounded variants, without claiming a model in which an exact time-version of the theorem holds. Status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Invariance and Universality of Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the Invariance Theorem and universality for Kolmogorov-style complexity measures.
status_evidence.claim: Standard expositions of the Invariance Theorem do not provide a time-complexity analogue with bounded additive overhead.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov complexity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Invariance theorem: complexities relative to two universal machines differ by at most an additive constant.
status_evidence.claim: Wikipedia presents only the length-based Invariance Theorem and does not record a time-bounded analogue.
